notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], lerobot-humanoid-model/models/bipedal_plateform/mjcf/scene.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's actuator_ctrlrange (twelve position actuators, scene.xml:10-21) before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The card's other models (the no-arms and lerobot_humanoide scenes, the fixed-base scene and the identification copies) are not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, and the upstream provides MJCF/URDF assets rather than a Python device class (README.md:40). MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the callable fake_mujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text and its includes for the model shape (actuator count, per-actuator control ranges, joint dimensions, option timestep) but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference. The lock names the same object as .fake:fake_mujoco.

MODEL AND SUBMODULE EVIDENCE: the model directories are git submodules; the pinned superproject commit records lerobot-humanoid-model as a gitlink (160000 commit ea23cbac9b79833eff974d9196a7edb8043effb6), so no Fact cites a line inside it (G4 reads the superproject tree and would report REF_MISSING). The nine Facts cite README.md lines of the superproject only, and the ctrl envelope is derived from the model at run time, not copied into a Limit. The model file is read from the read-only clone and is never copied into the package or imported.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the other MJCF variants, the runtime and identification stacks, and the hardware repository are not part of this driver; there is no viewer or rendering; no physical LeRobot humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives, which PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card scene, control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
